title: Death in Detention: Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias Dies in Laredo ICE Custody as Family Alleges Denied Medication

content:
Emiliano Andrade-Covarrubias, a 56-year-old Mexican national and longtime Dallas-area painting contractor, died Saturday morning inside a federal immigration detention facility in Laredo. He is the seventh person to die in ICE custody in Texas this year — and the second to die in an ICE facility in Laredo.

Staff at the Rio Grande Processing Center found Andrade-Covarrubias unresponsive in his cell during a routine security check at around 10 a.m. on Saturday, October 17, 2026, according to his daughter, Estefani Andrade, and U.S. Rep. Henry Cuellar, D-Laredo, who both confirmed the death to the Texas Tribune. Facility staff performed CPR and called emergency services. He did not survive.

The Rio Grande Processing Center is operated by GEO Group under contract with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. GEO Group and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security did not immediately respond to the Texas Tribune’s requests for comment on Sunday.

What the family says

Estefani Andrade, 29, a U.S. citizen, told the Tribune her father had spent decades in the Dallas area painting apartments and townhomes, raised three adult children, and had been traveling back and forth to Mexico, where he was building a house he hoped to settle in one day. He was detained in June after returning from Mexico by bus.

She said her father had a heart condition, diabetes, and high blood pressure — and that during four months in detention he told staff he was having trouble breathing and felt tightness in his chest. According to her account, staff repeatedly ignored his complaints and would not give him the medication he needed. The family noticed alarming weight loss on video calls.

Crucially, the family says they learned of his death not from any federal agency, but through the Webb County Medical Examiner’s Office, which is performing the autopsy. No cause of death has been released.

The pattern

The numbers put this death in grim context. Andrade-Covarrubias is the seventh ICE custody death in Texas in 2026. The year’s first — Geraldo Lunas Campos, at a facility in El Paso in January — was ruled a homicide by the El Paso medical examiner after guards restrained him until he stopped breathing. The second Laredo death this year: Felix Alcorta-Rodriguez, 63, who died June 19 after being found unresponsive at the Webb County Detention Center.

Cuellar visited the Rio Grande Processing Center on Sunday to ask what happened. Mexico’s government demanded a “prompt, thorough, and transparent” investigation; the Mexican foreign ministry raised the count to 18 Mexican nationals who have died in U.S. custody or during immigration operations since January 20, 2025, and expressed “deep concern” over the recurrence.

What Webb Watch 956 is asking

  • The Webb County Medical Examiner’s autopsy will determine cause and manner of death. Its findings should be public.
  • Did the facility follow federal detention standards for medical screening and medication continuity? GEO Group lists medical services among its contracted responsibilities. ICE’s own review process should answer this; the silence so far is not an answer.
  • Why did a grieving family learn about this death from the county morgue instead of the agency that held him?

The family’s allegations about denied medication are, at this point, allegations — reported by the daughter to the Texas Tribune and not yet confirmed or denied by the facility’s operator. They are serious enough to demand verification, not dismissal.
